nodes.title: World Action Models
nodes.body: A research topic exploring models that connect observations, possible actions, and predicted outcomes. Open the topic to inspect research questions, hypotheses, and evaluation gaps.

nodes.title: Dynamics
nodes.body: Models of how motion changes under forces and assumptions. Read the toy dynamics note and consider where its assumptions limit robot planning.

nodes.title: Optimization
nodes.body: Choosing solutions under objectives and constraints. Includes mathematical assumptions and links to trajectory planning; relevance does not establish a proof.

nodes.title: Algebra
nodes.body: Study algebraic structures such as groups. These reading notes remain independent of robotics unless an explicit connection is proposed.

nodes.title: World Action Models: research questions
nodes.body: Synthetic research outline: investigate how a learned model might connect observations, predicted dynamics and candidate robot actions. This outline proposes studying mechanics and optimization as foundations; it contains no validated performance claims.

nodes.title: A toy dynamics model
nodes.body: Synthetic teaching note: model motion under explicitly stated assumptions. A robot planning study could use this dynamics model, but applicability must be checked for the actual system.

fields.units: F in newtons; m in kilograms; a in metres per second squared.
assumptions: Constant mass; an inertial reference frame.
fields.validity: Teaching example only; not a validated model of a specific robot.

nodes.title: Optimization: assumptions before solutions
nodes.body: Synthetic theorem worksheet: before using an optimization result in robot planning, state its assumptions and proof obligations. This worksheet deliberately contains an unfinished proof.

fields.statement: Example exercise: establish a property of a chosen optimization problem.
assumptions: The problem and feasible set must be specified.
fields.proof: Incomplete exercise; no theorem is asserted as established.

nodes.title: Abstract algebra reading questions
nodes.body: Synthetic independent research notes on groups and algebraic structure. No robotics connection is asserted. This document demonstrates that independent fields belong in the same library.

nodes.title: Toy claim: prediction may aid planning
nodes.body: Synthetic hypothesis: a learned dynamics predictor may improve planning on the specified toy task. No general performance claim is established.

nodes.title: Toy experiment: missing validation
nodes.body: Synthetic evidence record: no controlled evaluation of the toy dynamics predictor has yet been performed. This is an evidence gap, not support for a performance claim.

nodes.title: Autonomy foundations
nodes.body: A synthetic cross-domain reading collection connecting robotics, mechanics and mathematics.
